summary: The note compares confit and smoking, two low-and-slow cooking and preservation methods, covering their history, techniques, flavor agents, health concerns, and modern and home adaptations. Confit cooks and preserves food submerged in fat, while smoking uses smoke's drying and antibacterial effects. Both have evolved from preservation necessity toward flavor development, with distinct health considerations for each.
one_line: Compares confit (cooking in fat) and smoking as low-and-slow preservation and flavor techniques, including history, health concerns, and modern uses.
key_facts: Confit comes from the French word "confire," meaning "to preserve," and was developed in France during the 16th century for meats like duck, geese, and pork.
Pierre de Lune wrote 'Le Cuisinier' on September 12, 1651, attributing confit's origins to the need to preserve meat for harsher months.
Arnaud Gervais explained on September 8, 2023 that duck confit involves curing meat in salt, then slowly cooking it in its own fat at around 200 degrees Fahrenheit.
Confit can be stored in its fat for weeks, if not months.
Emily Stratton, at the Global Culinary History Symposium on October 4, 2023, traced smoke preservation to the Paleolithic era.
Hot smoking cooks and smokes food simultaneously at 140 to 300 degrees Fahrenheit, while cold smoking only flavors and preserves at lower temperatures.
Jimmy Brooks showcased a 12-hour brisket smoking process at the Annual Smoke & Fire Festival on September 20, 2023.
Lisette Dupont noted on November 2, 2023 that fat in confit creates an anaerobic environment that hinders bacterial growth and extends shelf life.
Hickory gives a strong, bacon-like taste, applewood a milder sweet note, and mesquite an earthy sharpness, per Kent Harlow's November 6, 2023 lecture.
Sandra Li (December 1, 2023) cautions that confit adds significant saturated fat, though portion size and frequency can mitigate this.
Dr. Harish Kumar's study published September 29, 2023 explored Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) in smoked meats as a long-term consumption risk.
Helen Cho opened a New York restaurant on October 15, 2023 using fruit and vegetable confit with olive oil instead of animal fats.
Marcus Vinícius demonstrated modern smoke infusion methods like liquid smoke, smoked salts, and smoking guns in a workshop on November 10, 2023.
Home cooks use oven-confit, DIY smokers, and stovetop smoking kits to adopt these techniques.
